svg.title: AssignDestForUntargetedMove: where should this tray go?
svg.desc: A RETRIEVE job planned 'empty tray T21 out of bay B21' without saying where. This helper asks ResolveBlockingTrays for a parking spot, which may first move other trays out of the way, then turns those extra moves into events.
svg.metadata: ["Start: the request arrives. The map is working_state as the method first sees it; no events yet. Step through the method one table row at a time.", "Row 1. A move without a destination must at least name its tray, and that tray must exist in the current garage. In this example: T21 is in B21. (passes)", "Row 2. A tray with a car must end at a heading that allows a fast retrieve later; an empty tray may park any way. In this example: T21 is empty. (false)", "Row 3. Ask ResolveBlockingTrays for a parking spot. Steps 4 to 7 happen inside it, on a private copy of the garage. In this example: allow_waypoint_stash keeps its default, true. (call)", "Row 4. Search outward from the tray for the cheapest free parking node. The search may path through other trays; it returns the spot and the trays in the way. The nodes on that path (except the spot itself) become off-limits for blockers. In this example: Every free spot near B21 is boxed in. Suppose the search returns P24 via P23, with T23 in the way (T9 sits on the W25 route). (P24, 1 blocker)", "Row 5. Find a new spot for the first blocker that can be resolved. If that spot is blocked too, recurse into ResolveBlockingTrays with the root tray marked immobile. If no parking is reachable, try a waypoint stash (tier 2). In this example: W41, W22 and P23 are now off-limits for T23, but the target P24 is allowed: T23 can move one step deeper. (T23 -> P24)", "Row 6. Record the blocker's move and apply it to the private copy, so the next search sees the new layout. In this example: P23 is free in the private copy. (recorded)", "Row 7. Search again for the root tray. Repeat until a spot with nothing in the way is found, or fail (after the tier-2 waypoint stash). In this example: The best spot is now P23, with nothing in the way. (dest = P23)", "Row 8. Choose the heading (parking node: empty tray keeps its axis, loaded tray uses the preferred heading) and write the destination into the existing event. In this example: T21 faces 90 and so does P23. (dest set)", "Row 9. Turn the recorded blocker moves into real events: apply each, add it to the DAG, chain them in order, chain per tray, and add edges from earlier moves that free or use the same space (freeing_moves). In this example: Adds event 2, T23: P23 -> P24. first_tray_event[23] = event 2. (adds 1 event)", "Row 10. Apply the root move and make it wait for the last blocker move; update the per-tray chain and first_tray_event. In this example: Edge event 2 -> event 3: T23 must be gone before T21 arrives. (adds 1 edge)", "Row 11. Return. DoTrayAssignments skips its main blocking-tray loop for this event (continue), because its blockers were handled here. In this example: The main blocking-tray loop is skipped for this event. (success)"]
